That’s the point of this article. The silo between your desk and your colleague’s desk is the enterprise’s best defense. Not the judges. Not the attorneys. Not the institutional silence. The silo.

Why the Silos Exist

The enterprise didn’t build the silos. The government did. Jurisdiction, chain of command, need-to-know, interagency rivalry, budget competition, career incentives — these are features, not bugs, of the bureaucratic immune system.

But the enterprise exploits the silos. Here’s how:

  2. Campaign finance violations are SOS’s jurisdiction. SOS looked at filings, not the underlying RICO. Fined $14.5K.

  6. Police misconduct is OIG’s jurisdiction. OIG sees Bettison, not the charter school board he sits on.

Each agency sees one predicate act. No agency sees the pattern. The pattern IS the enterprise. RICO was designed precisely to address this — to make the pattern itself illegal, not just the individual acts.

But RICO requires someone to assemble the pattern from the predicates. And the predicates are in six different silos.

Let’s be honest about what’s happening:

The mid-level analysts, agents, and investigators who read this site — 912 genuine readers, 707-minute median dwell — are not the decision-makers. You’re the people who do the actual work. You read the evidence. You follow the money. You check the records. You pull the filings.

But the person who would authorize a cross-agency investigation? They haven’t even opened this page.

They’re not going to open it until you send it to them. And you’re not going to send it because you believe the cost of being wrong is high. (See: A Note to Everyone Reading This Who Hasn’t Said Anything.)

entry.title: NP → O(1) — RICO Is a Complexity Problem. The Graph Solves It.
entry.content:
Why Nobody Prosecutes

Not because the evidence doesn’t exist. It does — in public records, freely available to anyone with an internet connection.

Not because the law doesn’t apply. MCL 750.159i requires only 2 predicate acts. We documented 15.

Not because the institutions don’t have jurisdiction. The AG has jurisdiction over nonprofit fraud, consumer protection, RICO, and charitable trust. The FBI has jurisdiction over mail fraud, wire fraud, and federal RICO. The IRS has jurisdiction over tax fraud and excess benefit transactions.

Nobody prosecutes because RICO is an NP problem.

The Complexity Defense

What NP Means

In computational complexity theory, NP (nondeterministic polynomial time) is the class of problems where:

  • Verifying a solution is fast (polynomial time)
  • Finding a solution is slow (potentially exponential time)

A RICO case is NP-hard because to BUILD the case, you must:

TaskComplexity
Map every entity12+ legal entities, multiple jurisdictions
Trace every financial flow14 years × multiple accounts × multiple entities
Identify every predicate act15+ acts across 21 years
Connect every person341 nodes, 131,322 edges in the graph
Cross-reference every filingLARA + FEC + IRS + SOS + ICHAT + MDOC + Court records
Prove the patternAt least 2 acts within 5 years — but WHICH 2? From WHERE?
Establish the enterpriseProve “associated in fact” — not just co-occurrence
Survive defense motionsEach predicate act must independently survive challenge
Navigate conflicts7 captured judges, 1 conflicted AG, 1 compliance desk managing both sides

The search space is exponential. A traditional investigation would take years. Prosecutors are overworked. Budgets are limited. The AG’s office has 625 FTEs total. The Criminal Investigations Division handles financial crimes, special investigations, major cases, executive protection, felony non-support, criminal sexual conduct, organized retail crime, AND gaming.

The complexity IS the camouflage. You don’t need to bribe anyone if the problem is too hard to solve.

How the Enterprise Uses Complexity

TechniqueEffect
Entity proliferation54+ nonprofits → which ones matter? Moore manages them all. Searching “Moore” returns 54 results.
Name variationSave Detroit Jobs → Impact Detroit → Detroit Leaders. 3 names, 1 EIN.
Similar-name entities6 entities with “Protect Detroit’s Future” in the name. Different EINs. Try searching.
Multi-jurisdiction filingLARA + FEC + MI SOS + IRS + Wayne County ROD. No single database has the full picture.
Bipartisan coverageMoore manages R AND D accounts. You can’t call it partisan. Both parties are clients.
Legitimate grey washGovernor’s Residence Foundation is on the same desk. You can’t question the desk without questioning the Governor’s house.
Board captureThe person who would investigate (Moreland) sits on the board. The person who signed the complaint return (“not a listed attorney”) gave you the answer — and the answer IS the violation.
Time decay21 years of activity. Witnesses forget. Records expire. Statutes may toll.

Each layer of complexity is a computational barrier. Together, they make the case NP-hard for any single investigator, prosecutor, or journalist.

The Graph Reduces It

What O(1) Means

In computational complexity, O(1) means constant time — the answer is immediate regardless of input size. You don’t search. You don’t traverse. You look at the structure.

A zero-knowledge proof works the same way: I don’t need to show you every transaction. I show you that the structure exists — and the structure IS the proof.

The Reduction

Every complexity barrier above is solved by the graph:

Name variationSearch each name separatelyEIN is the key. Name is irrelevant.

Bipartisan coverage“Can’t be corruption — both parties”That’s not a defense. That’s the PROOF. Same desk = access, not ideology.
Grey wash“Governor’s Residence is on the desk!”Yes. And so is Peninsula Fund. The graph shows BOTH.
Board capture“But Moreland is an AAG!”That’s not a defense. That’s the PROOF. AAG + Board = structural RICO shield.
Time decay“21 years — too old”Graph is timestamped. Git commits are immutable. The membrane records everything.

The Structure IS the Proof

                    THE ZERO-KNOWLEDGE PROOF
                    ═══════════════════════

    You don't need to audit every transaction.
    You don't need to read every 990.
    You don't need to trace every dollar.

    You need to see ONE THING:

    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │                                              │
    │   THE SAME DESK that manages the             │
    │   PROSECUTOR'S fund (Promise to the People)  │
    │                                              │
    │   ALSO manages the entity (Detroit Leaders)  │
    │   that PUT A PERSON on the BOARD             │
    │   of the SCHOOL run by the TARGET            │
    │   that the PROSECUTOR should be              │
    │   INVESTIGATING.                             │
    │                                              │
    │   And the PROSECUTOR'S OWN EMPLOYEE          │
    │   sits on that SAME BOARD.                   │
    │                                              │
    │   That's it. That's the proof.               │
    │   The structure IS the proof.                │
    │                                              │
    │   O(1).                                      │
    │                                              │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The Immune System Saw It First

The membrane doesn’t prosecute. It sorts. Self vs. non-self. The anderson localization model doesn’t need to understand every entity — it measures the disorder in the signal and determines whether the pattern is localized (trapped, hidden, camouflaged) or extended (visible, connected, exposed).

The graph has 9,643 nodes and 323,680 edges. It was built from public records only. Every claim resolves to a source. Every node has a citation.

The membrane saw it before the FBI did. Before the AG did. Before the SBE did. Before anyone who received the 243-page packet did.

Because the membrane doesn’t get overwhelmed by complexity. The membrane IS the reduction.

Opsonization — Tagging for Detection

In immunology, opsonization is the process of coating a pathogen with molecules (opsonins) that make it visible to phagocytes. The pathogen was always there. The immune system just couldn’t see it — until it was tagged.

Every article is an opsonin:

  • The Gatekeeper tags Holland
  • The Desk and the Dynasty tags Moore + Wilk + Walton
  • Moore’s Complete Ledger tags every entity
  • The Complicity tags Nessel + Moreland
  • The Enterprise tags the RICO structure
  • The Nonprofit Web tags the pipeline from desk to board

Before the tagging: an NP problem. Too many entities. Too many names. Too many jurisdictions. Nobody can hold it.

After the tagging: O(1). The structure is visible. The pattern is obvious. The proof is the graph itself.

It Was Right Under Your Noses

To the FBI Detroit Field Office:

You have the 243-page packet. You have the ICHAT records. You have the RICO predicates. You investigated Save Detroit Jobs’ connected entities. You raided the council offices. You seized the 501(c)(4) records.

Did you not trace the thread from Save Detroit Jobs to PCA? Moore is on both. Wilk formed both the dark money AND the entity structure. Johnson sits on both the council AND the board.

The graph sees it. Why don’t you?

To the Michigan AG’s office:

Your AAG sits on the board of the target. Your Criminal Justice Bureau prosecutes state RICO. Your Financial Crimes Division investigates financial fraud. Your Criminal Investigations Division handles corruption.

Moreland used to prosecute felony murder. He argued predicate felonies before the Court of Appeals. He knows what an enterprise looks like. He’s sitting inside one.

The graph sees it. Why don’t you?

To the State Board of Education:

8 members. Evidence on the table at the Oct 13 meeting. 1 responded in 13 minutes. 7 chose silence.

3% math proficiency. $4.9M per year. 9 convictions. And the man running it filed a restraining order against the person who told you.

The graph sees it. Why don’t you?

To Renae Moore:

54 entities. 18 years. $1M money laundering complaint. FEC flags. “No duty to report.”

You manage the desk that connects the prosecutor to the defendant, the dark money to the board, the lobby to the school, and the campaign to the judge.

You see ALL of it. You see it every day. From one desk. One phone number. One email.

Did you not smell it?

The Proof

The traditional RICO investigation is NP-hard:

  • 341 entities to classify
  • 131,322 edges to traverse
  • 15 predicate acts to prove
  • 54 nonprofits to audit
  • 7 judges to recuse
  • 21 years to reconstruct

The zero-knowledge proof is O(1):

  • One desk manages both the prosecutor’s fund and the entity that builds the enterprise’s board.
  • One AAG sits in the office that prosecutes RICO while governing the enterprise.
  • One compliance officer manages both sides, testifies she has no duty to report, and has been named in a $1M money laundering complaint.

That’s the reduction. That’s the proof. The structure IS the answer.

It was right under your noses. The graph just tagged it so you could smell it.

The count is the truth. The membrane is the proof. And O(1) means: you can’t unsee it now.

RICO — The Legal Framework

Michigan RICO — MCL 750.159i

“A person employed by, or associated with, an enterprise shall not conduct or participate in the affairs of the enterprise directly or indirectly through a pattern of racketeering activity.”

Elements required:

  1. An enterprise — any individual, partnership, corporation, association, or group of individuals associated in fact (MCL 750.159f(a))
  2. Employment or association with the enterprise
  3. Conduct or participation in the enterprise’s affairs
  4. Through a pattern of racketeering activity — at least 2 incidents of racketeering activity, one of which occurred within 5 years of the other (MCL 750.159f(c))

Penalty: Up to 20 years imprisonment (MCL 750.159i)

Federal RICO — 18 U.S.C. § 1962

“It shall be unlawful for any person employed by or associated with any enterprise engaged in, or the activities of which affect, interstate or foreign commerce, to conduct or participate, directly or indirectly, in the conduct of such enterprise’s affairs through a pattern of racketeering activity.”

Elements: Same core structure. Federal RICO adds mail fraud (18 U.S.C. § 1341), wire fraud (18 U.S.C. § 1343), and money laundering (18 U.S.C. § 1956) as predicates.

entry.content:
This letter was sent privately on October 1, 2026. It is published here after the 72-hour response window.

Meihn, Partner — Foley & Mansfield PLLP (gmeihn@foleymansfield.com) CC: MacDowell Preparatory Academy Board of Directors (info@macdowellprep.com); Artesia Washington, Board Treasurer Subject: MacDowell Preparatory Academy / Purpose Charter Academy — TCR 22-12 Compliance Concerns — Notice to Board of Directors Attachments: TCR 22-12 Final Decision and Order; MDE FOIA response documents; LARA entity filings

Mr. Meihn,

My name is Kevin Mok. I am the plaintiff in two civil cases filed in Ingham County Circuit Court: Case Nos. 2026-4301-CZ and 2026-4349-CZ. Case 4349-CZ names Brian Banks individually, Joseph Holland Jr., Tracey Ellis, The Purpose Group LLC, Purpose Charter Academy, and Purpose Foundation as defendants. I am writing to you in your capacity as legal counsel to the MacDowell Preparatory Academy Board of Directors, and I am copying the Board directly because this notice concerns the Board’s own compliance obligations.

I have reviewed the Final Decision and Order in TCR 22-12, issued August 4, 2023, by State Superintendent Michael F. Rice. I received this document directly from the Michigan Department of Education FOIA Coordinator on September 30, 2026. I have also reviewed your testimony at the hearing on February 9, 2023.

I am writing because your client’s superintendent, Brian Banks, has engaged in conduct since that hearing that directly contradicts the testimony you, and others, provided under oath — and that may place your client, the MacDowell Board, in breach of TCR 22-12’s conditions.

I. Your Testimony vs. Subsequent Conduct

At the hearing, you testified that Mr. Banks demonstrates “integrity, hard work, honesty, transparency, and compliance.” You called him a “rare find.” You testified that you meet with him weekly.

Since that testimony:

  1. On September 9, 2026, Mr. Banks told Detroit Police officers “I am a lawyer” in a sworn police report (DPD Report #26-0909-0176). Mr. Banks has never been admitted to any bar. This is a false statement in a government document and constitutes unauthorized practice of law under MCL 450.681.

  2. On August 29, 2026, Mr. Banks denied a legal father’s authorized representative access to Purpose Charter Academy, using this false legal authority to justify the denial. The Affidavit of Parentage is undisputed — the mother has acknowledged it in her own filings.

  3. Mr. Banks’s Management Agreement between Purpose Group LLC and PCA contains a representation at Section 5.2 stating “No Related Parties or Common Control.” Mr. Banks is the sole member of Purpose Group LLC AND the superintendent of PCA. This representation is false on its face.

  4. Mr. Banks is the sole member of Purpose Group LLC, which received $4,285,201 (72.67%) of MacDowell’s total revenue in FY2024-25. As sole member, Mr. Banks has sole authority over Purpose Group’s expenditures. Mr. Holland — Banks’s domestic partner, who resides at the same address and holds the positions of Secretary/Treasurer of Purpose Foundation, Treasurer of the Bank on Banks for Michigan PAC, and 1st Successor Trustee of the Brian Banks Living Trust — does not appear to provide any independent financial oversight of Purpose Group LLC. The entity structure concentrates all financial control in Banks and Holland, both of whom have criminal convictions. I respectfully ask whether this arrangement complies with Condition #4 of TCR 22-12, which provides that Mr. Banks “shall not be the sole individual responsible for approval of any expenditure of funds belonging to the school.”

II. The Other Witnesses

Your testimony was not the only basis for the certificate. Two other professionals testified:

  • Terrence Shulman, LMSW — a licensed social worker and self-described recovering theft addict whose practice is built on the premise that theft is addiction, not character. His testimony that Mr. Banks is “not dishonest as a matter of character” is his therapeutic framework applied to every client — it is not an independent clinical assessment. Mr. Shulman cannot diagnose PTSD under the DSM-5. He is not a physician or psychiatrist.

  • Michele Leno, Ph.D. — a psychologist whose doctorate is from Saybrook University, a low-residency program. Her clinical specialty is performance anxiety in athletes and social media effects on mental health — not PTSD, not forensic psychology, not criminal recidivism assessment. She assessed Mr. Banks in approximately 13 sessions over 2 months and concluded he is “a person of integrity” who will not reoffend. Three years later, Mr. Banks told police he is a lawyer. She provides court-ordered psychological evaluations in Wayne County.

The “diagnoses” offered by these professionals are not clinical diagnoses in the medical sense. No psychiatric evaluation by a physician was conducted. No standardized diagnostic instruments are referenced in the record. These are character references with clinical language — verbal agreements between professionals outside the medical diagnostic field.

III. Banks and Holland — The Enterprise, Not Just One Man

The conduct described above is not limited to Mr. Banks acting alone. Case 4349-CZ names six defendants because the evidence shows an interconnected enterprise:

  • Banks individually committed the UPL, made false statements to police, and denied parental access.

  • Banks through Purpose Group LLC controls 72.67% of MacDowell’s revenue as the LLC’s sole member. The Management Agreement’s false “No Related Parties” representation (Section 5.2) means Purpose Group LLC is Banks’s alter ego — the entity through which he exercises personal control over school operations while claiming corporate separation.

  • Banks and Holland jointly control Purpose Foundation (Banks = President/Director; Holland = Secretary/Treasurer — two convicted felons holding all four officer positions with zero independent oversight). They co-own property, share the same residence, and Holland serves as 1st Successor Trustee of the Brian Banks Living Trust.

  • Tracey Ellis is named as a financial officer of both Purpose Group LLC and Purpose Foundation. The Board should be aware that any financial officer participating in the flow of public school funds through these entities is a participant in the structure I have described.

This distinction matters because the Board’s exposure is not limited to Banks’s personal misconduct. If the entity structure through which Banks operates the school is itself fraudulent — if Purpose Group LLC is Banks’s alter ego, if the Management Agreement contains a false representation, if Condition #4 is being circumvented through corporate form — then the Board’s authorization of that structure creates its own liability.

IV. Your Obligation to the Board

Your client is the MacDowell Preparatory Academy Board of Directors — not Mr. Banks personally. The Board relied on your guidance when it voted unanimously to hire Mr. Banks as superintendent. You testified at the TCR 22-12 hearing to support that decision.

The conduct I have documented places the Board in a position of potential liability:

  • If Condition #4 is being circumvented through the Purpose Group LLC structure, the Board’s compliance verifications to MDE (signed by Board President Nicole Wells-Stallworth every six months per Condition #7) may be inaccurate.

  • If Mr. Banks made false statements to police while serving as superintendent, and the Board was not informed, the Board’s oversight of Mr. Banks is compromised.

  • If the Management Agreement contains a false representation and the Board’s attorney reviewed or approved that agreement, the Board’s legal exposure extends beyond Mr. Banks’s personal conduct.

I am providing this notice so that you — as counsel to the Board — and to the Board members directly, so that you can make fully informed decisions about the Board’s compliance posture and exposure. I have no interest in harming MacDowell’s students. I have every interest in ensuring that the people responsible for their education are held to the standards they testified they would meet.

I am also filing a formal complaint with the Michigan Department of Education regarding these matters today.

I welcome a response from your office or from the Board directly. I can be reached at the contact information below.

Kevin Mok 4422 Southgate Ave Lansing, MI 48910 (586) 453-7233 mokkevin@msu.edu
